Bushfood, Stories and Culture on the Menu in Dumbleyung

By
Have a Go News
-
04/08/2026
Share
Facebook
X
Linkedin
Email
Print
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 2:32
    Instaread

    A unique dining experience celebrating Noongar culture, native bush foods and the rich heritage of Western Australia’s Great Southern will take centre stage in Dumbleyung this September as part of the 2026 Bloom Festival.

    The Dumbleyung Bushfood Dinner will be held on Saturday, September 26, at the Dumbleyung Town Hall, bringing together visitors and locals for an evening of exceptional food, storytelling and cultural connection.

    Hosted by Wuddi Aboriginal Cultural Tours in partnership with Gather Foods, the event is supported by the Western Australian Indigenous Tourism Operators Council (WAITOC) and promises a contemporary menu inspired by traditional Aboriginal ingredients sourced from the Great Southern region.

    Known for showcasing native Australian flavours, Gather Foods will create a bespoke dining experience highlighting the diversity of bush foods while celebrating thousands of years of Noongar knowledge and cultural practice.

    Guests will also enjoy storytelling, displays of local artefacts and insights into the enduring relationship between Noongar people, food and Country, offering a deeper understanding of Aboriginal culture beyond the dinner table.

    WAITOC Business Development Manager Briony Arnold said the event highlights the important role Aboriginal tourism plays in sharing culture and supporting local communities.

    “The Dumbleyung Bushfood Dinner is a wonderful example of Aboriginal tourism at its best, bringing together cultural storytelling, local food traditions and community connection,” Ms Arnold said.

    “Events like this give visitors and locals the opportunity to experience Noongar culture through food while learning about the deep knowledge and history that Noongar people hold about Country.”

    She said WAITOC was proud to support initiatives that created meaningful cultural experiences, generated opportunities for Aboriginal businesses and encouraged visitors to engage with Western Australia’s diverse Aboriginal cultures.

    The Bushfood Dinner forms part of the Great Southern’s month-long Bloom Festival, which celebrates the region’s spectacular wildflowers, local communities, food experiences and cultural heritage each spring.

    Dumbleyung is located around a three-hour drive south-east of Perth, making the event an ideal weekend escape for those looking to combine regional travel with a memorable culinary experience.

    Tickets are available through Humanitix, with prices starting from $152 per person, while discounted group bookings are available for six or more guests.

    Event Details

    • Event: Dumbleyung Bushfood Dinner
    • Date: Saturday, 26 September 2026
    • Time: 5pm to 9pm
    • Location: Shire of Dumbleyung Town Hall, Dumbleyung WA
    • Cost: $152 pp + booking fee, or for Group Bookings of 6 or more $145pp + booking fee
    • Hosted by: Wuddi Aboriginal Cultural Tours and Gather Foods
      as part of the 2026 Bloom Festival
